context_requirements: Expression of the targeted ATPase (e.g. SERCA/ATP2A, Na+/K+-ATPase ATP1A1/ATP1B1, or vacuolar H+-ATPase) at levels sufficient for inhibition at 10 uM
Intact ER calcium stores and ER stress/UPR signalling capacity (ATF6, PERK, IRE1 arms)
For apoptosis readouts, functional caspase activation and, for some lines, TP53-independent death pathways
For cholesterol-synthesis suppression, active SREBP-2/HMGCR pathway (hepatocyte-like lines)
falsifiers: No induction of UPR/ER-stress landmark genes (e.g. HSPA1A, DNAJB1, HERPUD1, XBP1, ATF5) at 6 h in any of the nine lines
No suppression of cholesterol-synthesis genes (HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, EBP) at 6-24 h
No late decrease in proliferation/G2-M genes (CCNB1, CDK1, AURKA, TOP2A) at 24 h
No apoptosis-associated changes (PMAIP1, BAX, GADD45A) at 24 h
A response pattern indistinguishable from generic cytotoxic stress across all lines

evidence.supports: ER Ca2+-ATPase inhibition by thapsigargin raises cytosolic Ca2+ and triggers apoptosis with DNA fragmentation
Ca2+-ATPase inhibition induces caspase-3 activation and PARP cleavage, linking ATPase inhibition to apoptosis
Vacuolar H+-ATPase inhibition causes lysosomal dysfunction and caspase-3-dependent apoptosis
ER Ca2+-ATPase inhibition (thapsigargin) induces neuronal apoptosis, confirming ATPase-inhibitor-driven cell death
Mitochondrial F1Fo-ATPase inhibitor (IF1) modulation alters ATP hydrolysis and ROS, indicating ATPase inhibition affects metabolic/oxidative stress programs
